item.title: bj-1: close hook: atm-task-close.py roles dev, fix, sanity, qa; task-close-vars.j2, sanity-fail.xml.j2, rebase-required.xml.j2; max_sanity_rounds

results.statement: When a dev or fix bead closes, the group's sanity bead must be assigned to the dev-sanity member with the sanity template and vars without any lead action: by the dev's close hook in the same shell command as bd close, and by atm-bd when bd ready lists the sanity bead with no ATM task.
results.quote: the first issue to solve is mechanical.  when dev or fix bd is closed, sanity 'bd ready' is true.  the atm-bd cron/console will 'atm task assign <bead-id> <sanity-agent> --template <template> --args <vars> automatically.  This assignment must be done --as <phase-lead>
results.context: phase-bj planning 2026-10-18: Rand's close-hook and mechanical-assignment rulings (atm-core #1873 comment 1, atm-bd-orchestration #340, PR #342)
results.deterministic_check: close a dev bead through the hook in a scratch repo and read atm task list: the sanity task exists before the hook exits; kill the hook between its commands and one atm-bd tick assigns it

Two things must be planned in the item: a close hook or close script that, when a dev or fix bead closes, runs the sanity bead's task assignment in the same shell command as bd close; and atm-bd assigning the sanity bead on its own when bd ready lists it and it has no ATM task. A statement of intent such as 'sanity should be automated' or 'smoother hand-off' is not the mechanism. A notice, report, or message is not an assignment. Judge whether the mechanism is present, not whether anything conflicts with it.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` commit to an approach for sanity assignment that differs from the one `anchor.statement` requires? Look for an explicit statement in the item that a person (for example the lead) performs or triggers a sanity assignment, that the close hook does not assign, that atm-bd does not assign ready sanity beads, that only a notice is sent, or that some kind of bead (dev or fix) is left out. A script or hook that runs the assignment under the phase lead's identity (for example `atm task assign ... --as <phase lead>`) is not a lead action; a lead action is the lead personally performing, approving, or triggering the step. An item that does not mention sanity assignment at all, or mentions it only as a goal, does not differ from the anchor. Judge conflict only.

results.statement: The sanity close hook must count FAIL rounds per sanity bead in metadata.sanity_round and, when the count reaches max_sanity_rounds from the repository configuration (default 5 when unset), must escalate to the phase lead instead of reopening the checked bead.
results.quote: sure, we can have sanity keep a counter and when count exceeded escelate to team-lead.  I would default max-sanity to ~5 if not overridden in atm-bd repo git settings.
results.context: phase-bj planning 2026-10-18: Rand's close-hook and mechanical-assignment rulings (atm-core #1873 comment 1, atm-bd-orchestration #340, PR #342)

The plan may state these as rules or as a worked sequence of rounds, for example the fifth FAIL escalating when nothing is configured and a configured value of 2 escalating on the second FAIL. Judge presence of this plan only, not conflict.

criteria.no: Nothing in the item is irreconcilable with the rule: it follows the rule, says nothing about the round limit, or plans only behaviour the rule allows.
criteria.unclear: The item might or might not conflict with the rule; its wording does not settle it.
criteria.yes: The item plans behaviour that cannot be reconciled with the anchor's round-cap rule.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` state a plan that cannot be reconciled with `anchor.statement`? The anchor requires that once a sanity bead's FAIL count reaches the repository's `max_sanity_rounds` (5 when unset) the hook escalates to the phase lead rather than reopening the checked bead. A plan conflicts if it says FAILs are reopened without limit, never escalates, hard-codes the cap with no repository setting, uses a different default, or waits until the count exceeds the cap. A plan that describes reopening on a FAIL but says nothing about a round limit is silent about the cap, not in conflict. Judge conflict only.

results.statement: atm-task-close.py must take its input as one sc-compose --vars file that carries every value the role needs, must validate it by rendering a header-only j2 template in strict mode before any check runs, and must pass that same file unchanged to the atm task assign and atm send templates it runs.
results.quote: the hook has vars specified by the hook python.  the hook input vars should be sc-compose --vars payload with every setting necessary to complete everything inside the hook.  the input to the hook would verify vars against pydantic model and reject any missing/unpopulated vars you could define this as a 'special unrendered sc-compose j2 w/ only compined header' so validation is trivial.  (this would skip the need for a pydantic model).  the same vars could be sent to ... same vars sent to 'atm ... --template --vars <shared-vars>'  and sc-compose bead ... --template --vars <shared-vars>
results.context: phase-bj planning 2026-10-18: Rand's close-hook and mechanical-assignment rulings (atm-core #1873 comment 1, atm-bd-orchestration #340, PR #342)
results.deterministic_check: a vars file missing commit fails before any git or gh call with an err naming commit; the assign and send subprocess argv carry --vars <the same path>

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` state an approach for atm-task-close.py's own input that `anchor.statement` rules out? Ruled out for the hook: taking its values from anything other than one sc-compose --vars file (command-line flags, environment, several files); validating them with a separately defined schema or model of the hook's fields instead of the header-only template render; validating only after checks have started; giving the assign or send templates a rebuilt, edited, or second vars set instead of the same file. Leaving a part out or naming only some of the commands is not a conflict either. Judge conflict only.
